Enderby refuses, pleading hard times, heavy taxes, and shattered fortunes to shepherd for his children. Lord Rippingdale sneers that this is treason and calls him miserly. Enderby answers that plain John Enderby can serve king and children better than Sir John. Charles wavers, but Rippingdale, his enemy of ten years, presses the attack. Parker opens a Cavalier-era story of honor, money, and court spite.
nasa-tm-19700026301-impulsive-orbit-tran:
Ivan L. Johnson Jr. of the Mathematical Physics Branch wrote this internal note on April 12, 1968. It was issued by the Manned Spacecraft Center in Houston. It treats the best use of short engine burns to move between orbits, using a faster form of the gradient method.

Johnson first states the transfer problems, then describes a digital computer program for improving chosen parameters. Two-body motion is handled through a universal variable formulation, with trajectory derivatives worked out for the search. Earlier methods tried in his section, including steepest descent and second order schemes, are recalled along the way. The method is finally applied to an optimal transfer flown with three separate burns.
nicholas-nickleby:
Charles Dickens began Nicholas Nickleby within a few months of finishing the Pickwick Papers, he says in his preface. The full title promises the fortunes, misfortunes, and complete career of the Nickelby family. Dickens uses the preface to attack a real abuse behind the tale.

Cheap Yorkshire schools, he writes, were then common, though few survive now. Any man unfit for other work could open a school with no test of skill. Surgeons, chemists, and bakers all had to prove their craft, but schoolmasters did not. Dickens calls those Yorkshire masters the lowest round in the ladder. His novel grew, in part, from that charge.
podcast-joerogan-fmZ4CgDC_bY:
Rogan and comedian Theo Von get real in a segment of the Joe Rogan Experience about depression, ayahuasca, and anxiety in the genes. Von is famous for surreal jokes, but his talks with Rogan often turn to the heavy stuff he grew up around. Two comics discuss pain without flinching.

They compare family histories of addiction and low moods, and what plant medicine did or did not do for them. The laughs keep coming through the dark, which is the pair's gift. The segment is a candid, funny record of how two funny men talk when the subject is their own wiring.
podcast-joerogan-u1jlt0nTHbY:
Jonathan Zimmerman joins Joe Rogan to tell what he learned in two years of life in Nepal in a segment from the show. Zimmerman went to the Himalayan land and stayed long enough for it to change him. He brings those lessons to Rogan.

Zimmerman tells of monks, peaks, and a pace of life far from the US rush. He shares what the stay taught him about want, calm, and the self. Rogan asks what he brought home that still holds. Listeners get a travel tale with a soul. The library holds the segment as an archive record of his account.
podcast-tuckercarlson-wNk9oD8abBY:
A former CIA agent joins Tucker Carlson to speak out on a sweep of dark files. The title names JFK, the 2001 attacks, UAPs, Martin Luther King Jr., MKUltra, and all he says Trump hides. The guest is not named in the title.

The guest gives his read on each case in turn, drawn from his years in the agency as he tells it. He argues the state still seals the core of each tale. Carlson presses him on which claim he would stake his name on. Listeners get a whistleblower-style tour of the vault. The library holds the talk as an archive record.
poor-dear-margaret-kirby:
Kathleen Norris gathered her stories in this third volume of her works, opening with the title novella about a marriage gone cold. Margaret Kirby, married nearly seven years, reflects bitterly that she and her husband are as near hating each other as two civilized people ever were. The Kirbys have long since stopped discussing it. They ride home through winter twilight in her motor-car in silence, rich, handsome, and miserable.

Eighteen stories follow, with titles that map Norris's territory: Bridging the Years, the Tide-Marsh, What Happened to Alanna, Miss Mix, Kidnapper, Rosemary's Stepmother, and Rising Water. Norris wrote about money, marriage, and family duty for the great magazine public, especially women readers, and her gift was taking domestic stalemate seriously as drama. The title story's question, whether two people who have stopped speaking can start again, drives the whole collection.
sermons-at-rugby:
John Percival, Bishop of Hereford and once headmaster of Rugby, preached these sermons to the boys of that school. James Nisbet issued the set in London in 1905. Percival calls the pieces stray chips from a busy schoolmaster's workshop, gathered by a kind publisher.

No linked doctrine runs through the set. One sermon fits a church season, another a term's start or close, and many grew from some event in school life. Percival dedicates the book to his boys, his fellow masters, and past workers. The first sermon treats love of country joined with faith, opening on Jerusalem as a built city.
the-mirrors-of-downing-street-some-polit:
Political reflections titled The Mirrors of Downing Street, by A Gentleman with a Duster, the pen name of Harold Begbie, appear here only in their opening leaves. A portrait of David Lloyd George faces the title page. Putnam's Sons published the illustrated volume in New York and London in 1921, and no chapter text is present in these pages.

An epigraph from John Morley insists that right and wrong belong to the nature of things and that breaking their laws brings a penalty. A publishers' note follows, arguing that America and England, having fought a great war together in defence of civilization, now share duties. Protecting the liberties of smaller states and weaker communities heads that shared task.
the-trail-of-the-tramp-by-a-no-1-the-fam: The Trail of the Tramp was written by A-No. 1, who bills himself 'the famous tramp who traveled 500,000 miles for $7.61,' and published it himself at Erie, Pennsylvania, in an eighth edition priced at twenty-five cents. The pages present are advertising front matter: a portrait, an illustrations list by Joseph Earl Shrock, and instructions for buying his books from any news agent or train news butcher. The tramp's own road narrative begins beyond these leaves.
